content: A FORCE is a push or a pull.
Forces make things START moving, STOP moving, or CHANGE direction.
- The bigger an object, the more gravity it has
- A force that SLOWS DOWN movement
- Happens when two surfaces rub together
- Examples: brakes on a bike, shoes on floor
Law 1: Objects stay still (or keep moving) unless a force acts on them.
Example: A ball stays still until you kick it.
Example: Kick harder = ball goes farther.
Law 3: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Example: Push against a wall, wall pushes back!

listening_script.text:
A FORCE is a push or a pull.
Forces make things START moving, STOP moving, or CHANGE direction.
TYPES OF FORCES:
1. GRAVITY
- Pulls everything toward Earth
- Why objects fall down
- The bigger an object, the more gravity it has
2. FRICTION
- A force that SLOWS DOWN movement
- Happens when two surfaces rub together
- Examples: brakes on a bike, shoes on floor
3. MAGNETIC FORCE
- Attracts or repels magnetic materials
- Works without touching!
NEWTON'S LAWS (simplified):
Law 1: Objects stay still (or keep moving) unless a force acts on them.
Example: A ball stays still until you kick it.
Law 2: More force = more movement.
Example: Kick harder = ball goes farther.
Law 3: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Example: Push against a wall, wall pushes back!
Physics Vocabulary:
dictation: A FORCE is a push or a pull.
Forces make things START moving, STOP moving, or CHANGE direction.
